R062-01.notes: A takes one detail from the last paragraph and overstates it; the passage says synthetics fall short. C is off topic. D is only the first paragraph, and the passage never compares strengths. B covers both the mechanism and the history of the debate. Factual check: setae counts (~6.5M per tokay, so hundreds of thousands per toe, each with 100-1000 spatulae, billions overall), clinging in a vacuum, no glands, glass ruling out hooks, the hydrophilic/hydrophobic test (Autumn et al. 2002), humidity raising adhesion somewhat, peeling release, and the synthetics' self-cleaning gap are all accurate.

R062-02.notes: Direct detail. A, B and C are the evidence the passage gives for the other hypotheses (suction, hooks, water films). They make good mismatch traps.

R062-03.notes: The passage states the prediction directly: 'If water films were essential...far more strongly.' A reverses the logic. B is not addressed and contradicts the humidity note. D is unrelated. A careful reverse-logic item, but easy.

R062-04.notes: 'Though...somewhat' marks a concession: water helps a little, but van der Waals remains the main mechanism. B overstates. C is unsupported. D belongs to the next paragraph. 'Minor role' fits 'somewhat'.

R062-05.notes: 'Any single contact is feeble, but billions...' means weak. A and C are senses about people. B (unconvincing) is the 'feeble excuse' sense, which does not fit a physical contact.

R062-06.notes: Tape peels 'more easily' from one edge, just as setae detach a few at a time. 'Far less force' is slightly stronger than 'more easily', but 'almost absent in another [direction]' supports it. A is the literal-sticky trap that the passage's no-glue point contradicts. C confuses this with the durability point in the last paragraph. D is invented.

R062-07.notes: The mechanism needs the branch tips to come 'extremely close' to the surface, so a surface they cannot approach would weaken the grip. Case for B: humidity strengthens the grip somewhat, so a water-repelling surface might lose a little. But the test showed similar grip on both kinds of surface, so B is not 'most likely' harder. C contradicts the opening (geckos hold polished glass). D contradicts the vacuum result. A is the single best answer.

R062-08.notes: Paragraph 3 names capillary attraction from water films as the rival hypothesis. A and B were early guesses that had already been ruled out, not alternatives to the van der Waals explanation (note that the stem says 'alternative to van der Waals forces'). D is not in the passage.

R062-09.notes: 'Can now hold heavy objects...release them cleanly, though none yet matches...' means impressive but short of the gecko. A, B and C each contradict the text.

R062-10.notes: Direct detail from paragraph 4. B contradicts the no-glands point. C is unsupported. D is the opposite: pulling 'straight out' is the hard way, per the tape analogy.
